column1: 8.3.2 The Linearized IS Curve Equation (8.20) relates output to inflation in the form of the deviation around the level of output that would occur in the absence of nominal price rigidity. It forms one of the two key components of an optimizing model that can be used for monetary policy analysis. The other component is a linearized version of the household’s Euler condition, (8.7).
